findings.text: VM capability query gates protected-mode extensions then reports availability per extension: generic KVM and ARM features report present, hardware-gated features delegate to platform helpers for memory tagging, vector, performance, steal time, debug counts, address size and pointer authentication, while VM-specific queries return per-VM limits or settings and unknown extensions report absent.

vCPU admission rejects creation after interrupt controller initialization and identifiers beyond the VM limit; creation initializes timer, performance, paravirtual time and MMU state, allocates VGIC state and publishes shared pages with cleanup on failure; teardown releases memory caches, timer, performance, VGIC and ARM state with distinct paths for protected and conventional modes.

VM allocation returns a zeroed control structure using a physically contiguous allocator without VHE and a virtually contiguous allocator with VHE; the architecture device control entry unconditionally reports an invalid operation.

Per-vCPU VGIC state couples an active-interrupt queue and its lock, a private-interrupt array, a redistributor device descriptor with base address and owning region, and a virtual-PE LPI count; distributor state holds model selection, LPI table, region list and base addresses.

Private interrupt allocation is idempotent and sized by interrupt architecture generation; each slot starts detached with empty queue membership and zero references, software interrupts default enabled edge triggered while private peripherals default level triggered, and grouping plus routing defaults differ between legacy and versioned controller models.

Full pointer authentication requires host support plus exactly one implemented algorithm family where address authentication matches general authentication for both instruction and data keys across legacy and versioned feature fields.

Private allocation serializes on the VM configuration lock; redistributor assignment holds the slot lock outer and configuration lock inner; active-list retirement holds the per-CPU list lock with interrupts masked and nests each interrupt lock inside; deleted-LPI reclamation walks the LPI table under its lock with interrupts masked.

Redistributor devices start undefined and registration defers until a free region and valid base exist; success binds a region slot, derives a guest address by slot stride, publishes an MMIO device over a fixed two-page span and advances the region allocator; teardown clears the address and unregisters failed vCPUs inline while successful vCPUs defer unregistration to VM teardown.

VGIC address programming rejects reprogramming a defined address, requires alignment and overflow-free ranges within the physical mask and size limits, rejects distributor overflow, and rejects any overlap between the distributor window and any redistributor region whose size scales with online or configured vCPU count.

Teardown retires only message-based interrupts from the active queue by clearing pending state, unlinking the entry and dropping the owner reference; reference release applies solely to that class and signals when the last reference drops, after which unreferenced table entries are freed.

vCPU load refreshes VM identity and per-CPU context on vCPU change, orders timer load before interrupt controller load, then restores debug, trap, floating point, performance and steal-time state; wait-instruction traps adapt to global policy and single-task plus LPI activity, pointer-authentication traps honor nested state, and protected mode issues hypercalls while unsupported CPUs are flagged.

Unregistering a redistributor while holding the configuration lock during VM teardown inverts against source-read protection, so only creation-failed vCPUs unregister in the destroy helper and successfully published vCPUs must be unregistered elsewhere.

Capability results encode advisory vCPU count as the smaller of online CPUs and default maximum, maximum identifiers from per-VM limits when a VM is present, user-IRQ level one, register-range support limited to range zero, and per-redistributor MMIO span of two 64 KiB pages.

Guest performance support is present when the host performance list is non-empty; initialization numbers each counter slot, destruction disables and releases any bound host event per slot and synchronizes overflow handling, and counter lookup resolves an index to its descriptor.
ARM vCPU destruction unshares the vCPU page and any variable-sized vector-extension state, frees that state, and releases auxiliary register-cache allocations.
